meta.title: 16-QAM: constellation, EVM and symbol errors
meta.tools: Monte Carlo (NumPy), square-QAM SER theory, EVM measurement
meta.summary: Transmit Gray-mapped 16-QAM through AWGN, watch the constellation blur as SNR falls, and compare measured SER and EVM with 4(1−1/√M)Q(√(3E_s/((M−1)N₀))) and EVM = 1/√SNR.
meta.problem: 16-QAM carries 4 bits per symbol. How much more SNR does it need than QPSK, and how do engineers measure signal quality from a constellation?
meta.theory:
Square M-QAM: $P_s\approx 1-\left(1-2(1-\tfrac1{\sqrt M})Q\!\left(\sqrt{\tfrac{3E_s}{(M-1)N_0}}\right)\right)^2$. For M = 16 the minimum distance at
equal average energy is √(2/5)·√(2/…)… i.e. ~7 dB worse than QPSK at the same SER per symbol, ~4 dB per bit. Error-vector
magnitude (RMS) = $1/\sqrt{E_s/N_0}$ when noise is the only impairment.
meta.method: 10⁶ symbols per point, normalised to E_s = 1, Gray mapping per axis, minimum-distance decisions. EVM = √(mean|y−s|²/mean|s|²).

metrics.quantity: Extra Es/N0 needed vs QPSK for SER 10⁻³
